fullAnalysis: Pinpoint #687 looks broader than it really is because the board mixes atmosphere, transportation, shopping, and famous landmarks. "Fog" can feel especially loose on its own, and clues like "Cable cars" or "Alcatraz Island" could still sit inside a wider travel or California-themed guess. The clue that really tightens the set is "Golden Gate Bridge," because once that appears, the board stops feeling like a bag of tourist references and starts reading as one clean city picture.

From there, the answer resolves as San Francisco icons. The city is famously linked with bay fog and cable cars, while Ghirardelli Square, Alcatraz Island, and the Golden Gate Bridge are all unmistakable San Francisco landmarks. That reading explains the whole board more cleanly than broader labels like California attractions or tourist destinations, because every clue points back to the same city identity.
solutionNarrative: I did not have a clean category from the first clue. "Fog" felt too open, and even after "Cable cars" appeared, I could still justify a broader travel or transportation angle. "Ghirardelli Square" helped narrow the frame, but I still needed one clue that made the city connection impossible to miss.

That turning point was "Golden Gate Bridge." Once I let that clue lead the solve, the rest of the board stopped feeling scattered and started reading like a single San Francisco collage: fog, cable cars, Ghirardelli Square, Alcatraz Island, and the bridge itself. At that point, the city-specific reading explained the full set much better than any looser tourism label.

lessons.title: City boards often mix landmarks with atmosphere
lessons.body: A puzzle does not need every clue to be the same kind of thing. Weather, transportation, neighborhoods, and landmarks can all point back to one city.

lessons.title: Wait for the clue that makes the location unmistakable
lessons.body: Golden Gate Bridge is the clue that removes the ambiguity here. Once one clue makes the place obvious, go back and re-check the earlier references under that same frame.

lessons.title: Prefer the cleanest geographic fit over a broad travel label
lessons.body: A strong Pinpoint answer should explain why all five clues belong to the same place, not just why they feel like tourist-related words.
